sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
A mathematics bachelor’s degree can lead directly to this PhD. A 3.0 GPA and substantial proof-based
preparation are expected; the FAQ highlights real analysis, abstract algebra and linear algebra. International
applicants are eligible. [s2] [s3] [s6]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Prepare transcripts, a CV, the statement and three referees; apply through the graduate application system.
Submit early enough for referee invitations, which are sent only after submission. Obtain an English waiver or
qualifying scores. [s1] [s6] [s8]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
The statement asks for 1-4 relevant faculty; no prior signed supervisor agreement is listed. The strongest
verified match is analytic number theory. Confirm supervision capacity directly; no core algebraic-geometry or
representation-theory group was established in the reviewed roster. [s1] [s12]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
The graduate FAQ documents submission-triggered references, status tracking and correction of pending
reference requests. Allow several business days after submission before asking the department whether the
file is complete. [s8]
Cycle verification [Standing rule]
Standing admissions rules and 2026 sources were checked on November 5, 2026; no explicit Fall 2027
mathematics announcement was established. Many WSU pages blocked direct opening, so their official
indexed extracts were used and flagged. [s1] [s2] [s10]

sections.title: Deadlines by stage
sections.text:
Academic application; Funding consideration [Conflict]
The main mathematics page requires submission by December 10 at 8:59 p.m. PST for the following fall; the
Graduate School profile agrees on December 10. These are standing dates, not an explicitly labelled Fall 2027
announcement. An older departmental FAQ instead says January 10: use December 10 while seeking
confirmation. [s1] [s2] [s3]
Reference receipt; Test-score receipt; Supporting documents [Standing rule]
Complete the file for the December 10 review deadline. A separate later reference, score or
supporting-document deadline is not published in the reviewed instructions; submission triggers reference
invitations, so do not wait until the final evening. Self-reported optional GRE scores can be used initially; official
scores are required if admitted using them. [s1] [s8]

Accepting an offer [Standing rule]
The mathematics FAQ explicitly gives April 15 for accepting an offer. This is a standing departmental rule;
verify the date and any interim conditions in the actual Fall 2027 funding offer. [s3]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Conflict]
Mathematics lists TOEFL iBT 100 on the former scale, IELTS 7 or Duolingo 130. The central mathematics profile
distinguishes admission minima of 75/6.5/105 from assistantship minima of 100/7/130. Confirm the higher
mathematics/funding threshold and new-scale TOEFL equivalence; the general Graduate School new-scale
minimum is 4. Scores must be within two years. [s1] [s2] [s6]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
A completed US degree qualifies for an English-test exemption. The department also recognizes an
English-medium degree, whereas central rules should be checked for the documentation route. The reviewed
language says earned/hold a degree; treatment of a UChicago degree still in progress is not established. [s1]
[s6]
GRE General; GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
Both General and Mathematics Subject GRE scores are optional but encouraged, and should be under five
years old. This is a preference, not an indifferent or prohibited-score policy. [s1]

Transcripts and degree records [Conflict]
Upload current bachelor’s/master’s transcripts initially; official records are required after admission. Central
instructions require records from every institution, with original-language and English versions where
applicable, and do not require an outside credential evaluation. The department calls additional institutions
optional, so follow the broader central requirement pending clarification. [s1] [s6]
Mathematics-course list; Course descriptions [Standing rule]
Not listed as a separate required item on the public mathematics application checklist. This does not establish
whether the current portal permits an optional upload; exact prompt, length, formatting and upload/link rule
are not published. [s1]

sections.title: Recommendation letters
sections.text:
Number and type [Standing rule]
Three recommendations; provide each referee’s contact details, including email and telephone number. [s1] [s2]
Scholarship references [Standing rule]
The admission application automatically receives assistantship consideration. No separate standard
assistantship essay or extra reference is listed; other awards may impose their own requirements. [s2] [s3]
What sends the invitation; Before versus after submission [Standing rule]
The Graduate School FAQ says recommendation invitations are emailed only after the application is submitted.
Saving referee details alone is not enough under this published rule. [s8]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
The FAQ describes email notification when a recommendation arrives and recommendation status tracking in
the application’s Program Materials section. [s8]
Updating and reusing letters [Standing rule]
A still-requested recommendation can be edited or resent; a new referee can be added and the old request
deleted. Updating an already-submitted letter is not established. The FAQ describes a shared completed

application-material set accessible to multiple programs, but confirm whether a specific letter can be reused
for a new cycle. [s8]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Prior cycle]
A Fall 2027 mathematics stipend is not established. For historical context only, the 2024-26 collective
agreement lists a Pullman doctoral monthly rate of $2,437 and a 3% increase effective October 1, 2025:
$2,510.11 per month by arithmetic, or $22,590.99 over nine months. This is not a verified Fall 2027 offer or a
guarantee of summer pay. [s10]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Typical mathematics support is ten semesters/five years for bachelor’s entrants, with renewal subject to
progress. The handbook allows a request for a sixth year for entrants without a mathematics degree.
Appointments run August 16-December 31 and January 1-May 15; summer support is not guaranteed. [s3] [s4]
[s5]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
International students can receive assistantships. Central rules explicitly allow an international nonresident
tuition waiver throughout the assistantship-supported academic career; the domestic second-year residency
requirement must not be applied to an F-1 student. [s6] [s11]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
A half-time appointment normally means 20 hours weekly, full-time enrollment and a 3.0 GPA. Required
training and appointment paperwork apply. Tuition waivers and individual health insurance accompany eligible
appointments; current mandatory student fees should be confirmed because the mathematics benefits page
quotes 2023-24 figures. Passing the preliminary examination can raise the stipend in the following semester.
[s4] [s5] [s9] [s11]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
The admission application automatically receives assistantship consideration. No separate standard
assistantship essay or extra reference is listed; other awards may impose their own requirements. [s2] [s3]

Other funding routes [Standing rule]
Research assistantships may become possible after the second year. Summer teaching/research and
dissertation fellowships are possibilities, not guaranteed additions. Current award amounts, deadlines and
separate statements require confirmation. [s4]
Application fee [Standing rule]
The graduate application fee is $100 and nonrefundable. [s7]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
Central waivers include McNair and WSU REU participants: contact Raymond Herrera at raymond@wsu.edu
before applying. The mathematics FAQ’s limited underrepresented/DACA waiver is described for domestic
applicants and cannot be assumed available solely from F-1 status; ask the department about any other
current route before paying. [s3] [s7]

transcript wording is stricter/less inclusive than different central passages. Historical funding and fee figures
should not be promoted to 2027 values. International tuition-waiver eligibility is clarified by the current central
rule. [s1] [s2] [s3] [s4] [s6] [s11]

Confirm the Fall 2027 deadline, complete-file cutoff, in-progress US-degree waiver, new TOEFL assistantship
scale, actual stipend and student fees; ask whether submitted letters can be replaced and whether any
optional paper upload has a size limit. [s1] [s2] [s6] [s8]

reference requests. Allow several business days after submission before asking the department whether the
file is complete. [s8]
Cycle verification [Standing rule]

Deadlines by stage
Academic application; Funding consideration [Conflict]
The main mathematics page requires submission by December 10 at 8:59 p.m. PST for the following fall; the
Graduate School profile agrees on December 10. These are standing dates, not an explicitly labelled Fall 2027
announcement. An older departmental FAQ instead says January 10: use December 10 while seeking
confirmation. [s1] [s2] [s3]
Reference receipt; Test-score receipt; Supporting documents [Standing rule]
Complete the file for the December 10 review deadline. A separate later reference, score or
supporting-document deadline is not published in the reviewed instructions; submission triggers reference
invitations, so do not wait until the final evening. Self-reported optional GRE scores can be used initially; official
scores are required if admitted using them. [s1] [s8]

Accepting an offer [Standing rule]
The mathematics FAQ explicitly gives April 15 for accepting an offer. This is a standing departmental rule;
verify the date and any interim conditions in the actual Fall 2027 funding offer. [s3]
English and GRE
English requirement [Conflict]
Mathematics lists TOEFL iBT 100 on the former scale, IELTS 7 or Duolingo 130. The central mathematics profile
distinguishes admission minima of 75/6.5/105 from assistantship minima of 100/7/130. Confirm the higher
mathematics/funding threshold and new-scale TOEFL equivalence; the general Graduate School new-scale
minimum is 4. Scores must be within two years. [s1] [s2] [s6]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
A completed US degree qualifies for an English-test exemption. The department also recognizes an
English-medium degree, whereas central rules should be checked for the documentation route. The reviewed
language says earned/hold a degree; treatment of a UChicago degree still in progress is not established. [s1]
[s6]
GRE General; GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
Both General and Mathematics Subject GRE scores are optional but encouraged, and should be under five
years old. This is a preference, not an indifferent or prohibited-score policy. [s1]
Academic records
Transcripts and degree records [Conflict]
Upload current bachelor’s/master’s transcripts initially; official records are required after admission. Central
instructions require records from every institution, with original-language and English versions where
applicable, and do not require an outside credential evaluation. The department calls additional institutions
optional, so follow the broader central requirement pending clarification. [s1] [s6]
Mathematics-course list; Course descriptions [Standing rule]
Not listed as a separate required item on the public mathematics application checklist. This does not establish
whether the current portal permits an optional upload; exact prompt, length, formatting and upload/link rule
are not published. [s1]
Recommendation letters
Number and type [Standing rule]
Three recommendations; provide each referee’s contact details, including email and telephone number. [s1] [s2]
Scholarship references [Standing rule]
The admission application automatically receives assistantship consideration. No separate standard
assistantship essay or extra reference is listed; other awards may impose their own requirements. [s2] [s3]
What sends the invitation; Before versus after submission [Standing rule]
The Graduate School FAQ says recommendation invitations are emailed only after the application is submitted.
Saving referee details alone is not enough under this published rule. [s8]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
The FAQ describes email notification when a recommendation arrives and recommendation status tracking in
the application’s Program Materials section. [s8]
Updating and reusing letters [Standing rule]
A still-requested recommendation can be edited or resent; a new referee can be added and the old request
deleted. Updating an already-submitted letter is not established. The FAQ describes a shared completed

application-material set accessible to multiple programs, but confirm whether a specific letter can be reused
for a new cycle. [s8]
Written materials
Academic CV / resume [Standing rule]
A CV or résumé is required; no public length or formatting limit was established. Upload through the
application. [s1] [s2]
Statement of purpose; Research-interest statement [Standing rule]
Prepare a 1-2 page statement explaining motivation, mathematical/statistical interests and career goals,
naming 1-4 faculty of interest. Explain relevant nontraditional preparation or an adverse semester and what
you learned, if applicable. The public instructions do not specify font, spacing or margins. This is a paraphrase
of the linked prompt. [s1]
Personal / background statement; Research proposal; Publications list; Course-list document;
Scholarship essays; Other short answers / materials [Standing rule]
Not listed as a separate required item on the public mathematics application checklist. This does not establish
whether the current portal permits an optional upload; exact prompt, length, formatting and upload/link rule
are not published. [s1]
Writing sample / thesis / research summary [Standing rule]
Additional materials, including published papers, are explicitly welcomed as optional uploads with the
application. No separate thesis requirement, length limit or instruction to substitute links was established. [s1]
Funding and fees
Amount and coverage [Prior cycle]
A Fall 2027 mathematics stipend is not established. For historical context only, the 2024-26 collective
agreement lists a Pullman doctoral monthly rate of $2,437 and a 3% increase effective October 1, 2025:
$2,510.11 per month by arithmetic, or $22,590.99 over nine months. This is not a verified Fall 2027 offer or a
guarantee of summer pay. [s10]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Typical mathematics support is ten semesters/five years for bachelor’s entrants, with renewal subject to
progress. The handbook allows a request for a sixth year for entrants without a mathematics degree.
Appointments run August 16-December 31 and January 1-May 15; summer support is not guaranteed. [s3] [s4]
[s5]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
International students can receive assistantships. Central rules explicitly allow an international nonresident
tuition waiver throughout the assistantship-supported academic career; the domestic second-year residency
requirement must not be applied to an F-1 student. [s6] [s11]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
A half-time appointment normally means 20 hours weekly, full-time enrollment and a 3.0 GPA. Required
training and appointment paperwork apply. Tuition waivers and individual health insurance accompany eligible
appointments; current mandatory student fees should be confirmed because the mathematics benefits page
quotes 2023-24 figures. Passing the preliminary examination can raise the stipend in the following semester.
[s4] [s5] [s9] [s11]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
The admission application automatically receives assistantship consideration. No separate standard
assistantship essay or extra reference is listed; other awards may impose their own requirements. [s2] [s3]

Other funding routes [Standing rule]
Research assistantships may become possible after the second year. Summer teaching/research and
dissertation fellowships are possibilities, not guaranteed additions. Current award amounts, deadlines and
separate statements require confirmation. [s4]
Application fee [Standing rule]
The graduate application fee is $100 and nonrefundable. [s7]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
Central waivers include McNair and WSU REU participants: contact Raymond Herrera at raymond@wsu.edu
before applying. The mathematics FAQ’s limited underrepresented/DACA waiver is described for domestic
applicants and cannot be assumed available solely from F-1 status; ask the department about any other
current route before paying. [s3] [s7]
